title: Bank Return Reasons and the Base of the Payout Methods Return Charge
content:
When a transfer to a Payout Methods method is sent back, the receiving bank gives a reason, recorded on the return entry of the method's payout ledger as one of three return reasons: account closed, invalid account, or name mismatch. The base of the return charge follows the reason the receiving bank gave for the latest return on the method.

## Schedule of base amounts by return reason

| Return reason on the latest return on the method | Base of the return charge |
|---|---|
| Account closed | USD 20.00 |
| Name mismatch | USD 30.00 |
| Invalid account (any other reason) | The rail's own returned-payout fee |

## Notes to the schedule

1. **Which return.** The reason is read from the latest return on the method, the return the charge names. Reasons given on earlier returns to the same method are not read.
2. **Recorded reason.** The reason is the one the receiving bank gave, as recorded on the return entry.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Imagined latest return | Base of the return charge |
|---|---|
| International Wire Transfer returned with reason "account closed" | USD 20.00 |
| International Wire Transfer returned with reason "name mismatch" | USD 30.00 |
| International Wire Transfer returned with reason "invalid account" | The International Wire Transfer returned-payout fee |
| A method returned twice: first "name mismatch", latest "account closed" | USD 20.00, from the latest return |
